correctness.rationale: The two legality clauses are equivalent to increasing row downsets and suffix upsets. Selecting independent upper-tail thresholds a,b in the existential clause tests (a,b) in D_i; selecting a+1,b+1 in the universal clause tests the complement of (a,b) in the upset S_i, including empty tails. Heredity and induction extend depth-one agreement to all formulas; an empty existential input always gives false. The mandatory maximal and last-occurring pairs and the allowed intersection D_i∩S_i are necessary and sufficient: take downward closures row by row and use reverse induction on suffix unions. Each of the n−1 nonlast rows can contribute at most n²−1 free bits, attained by full shadows with the final row fixed to the full product and earlier rows containing the top pair. This covers n=1 (no free rows). Independent direct enumeration of n=2 using the quantified clauses reproduced the common modal/shadow partition and every fiber count, without executing checker.py.
residual_risks: The independent enumeration covers n=2 only, not the recorded n=3 sampling. The proof concerns pointwise agreement on one fixed labeled chain, not logic validity equivalence.

value.rationale: Knowing which accessibility data can actually be recovered from the two operations matters for comparing presentations of the same semantics. The theorem gives explicit least and greatest frames, locates every dispensable tuple, and measures the worst-case ambiguity exactly. This is a natural structural classification, not a two-world census presented as a general contribution.
residual_risks: The significance is within labeled finite-chain semantics; no claim about arbitrary relational languages or frame validity is needed.
